pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

3. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.

10. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Producers
   D. Tertiary consumers

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Ice melting to water

2. C — Glucose and oxygen

3. B — 100 °C

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

5. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

10. C — Producers

11. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

12. C — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Metals and Alloys; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water hardness; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Nutrition in animals; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reproduction in plants; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
